scope: Six exact-NCT observed Phase 3 readouts newly reconciled PRE to POST; clinical outcome observations are not prospective scores.
sourcePolicy: Issuer-primary and peer-reviewed sources dated on/before 2026-11-06. No unsupported numerical RAAS or clinical success probability.

facts.evidence: Praxis reported ulixacaltamide was generally well tolerated across Essential3, with no drug-related serious adverse events; this is issuer-reported and does not establish pooled rare-event risk.
Two Essential3 Study 1 key secondary endpoints (patient/global clinical impression and rate of improvement) were reported significant (p<0.001); the first Study 2 secondary was p=0.0042.

Study 1 reported significant patient global impression of change (PGI-C) and clinical global impression of severity (CGI-S) measures at Week 8; exact patient-centered benefit and MCID require separate assessment.
Issuer-reported mADL11 primary mean improvement 4.3 points at Week 8 (p<0.0001) in Study 1; a comparator-adjusted MCID assessment was not independently completed.
Issuer reported improvement appearing from Week 2 and persisting through Week 12 of the Phase 3 study; multi-year sustained benefit and long-term tolerability remain unestablished.

ASCO 2026 reported grade-3-or-higher ALT/AST elevations and anemia with the bezuclastinib/sunitinib combination; ALT/AST led to dose reductions in 13.2% and discontinuations in 1.5%. This is a risk observation, not a favorable safety score.
Exact-NCT PEAK report observed objective response 46% for bezuclastinib/sunitinib versus 26% with sunitinib alone; secondary efficacy observation, not future prediction.

Cogent reported the PEAK progression-free survival benefit irrespective of primary versus secondary KIT mutations. This is a descriptive subgroup report, not proof of a prospectively powered interaction test.

PEAK observed median PFS 16.5 vs 9.2 months (hazard ratio 0.50; 95% CI 0.39–0.65; p<0.0001), an objective observed benefit magnitude. Independent clinical-significance and external-validity review remains separate.

Cogent reported FDA NDA acceptance and Priority Review for bezuclastinib/sunitinib GIST treatment with a November 30, 2026 PDUFA goal date; this is an application-level milestone, not efficacy approval.

The issuer reported FDA accepted the GIST NDA for bezuclastinib/sunitinib with priority review and a November 30, 2026 PDUFA goal date. Approval, final FDA decision and comparative regulatory benefit-risk were not established as of this evidence date.

HAELO issuer described all observed TEAEs at Feb 10, 2026 cutoff as mild to moderate; no serious adverse events in 52 participants receiving lonvo-z. Rare or long-term gene-editing risks are not ruled out.
HAELO issuer reported all key secondary endpoints statistically significant (p<0.0001), including 62% attack- and therapy-free for Weeks 5–28 in the treatment arm versus 11% on placebo.

HAELO observed a monthly attack rate of 0.26 with lonvo-z vs 2.10 with placebo (87% relative reduction, p<0.0001). This is an observed clinical effect, not an independently calibrated FDA probability.
HAELO six-month randomized observation (Weeks 5–28) showed reduced attack rates. Multi-year durability of this one-time gene edit has not been established by these Phase 3 data alone.
As of the February 10, 2026 HAELO cutoff, issuer observed no serious adverse events among the 52 lonvo-z participants; this is sample-limited and does not establish freedom from rare serious risks.

Intellia announced that it had initiated rolling BLA submission for lonvo-z in HAE on April 27, 2026. A rolling submission is not equivalent to an FDA-accepted complete application or assigned PDUFA date.
ORBIT Phase 3 fracture-rate primary was not met, although a bone mineral density secondary endpoint improved significantly. Secondary BMD is not a substitute for annualized fracture-rate efficacy.
ORBIT Phase 3 did not show statistically significant annualized clinical fracture rate reduction versus placebo despite BMD improvement; clinical fracture benefit remains unproven.
COSMIC Phase 3 fracture-rate primary not met; secondary bone mineral density improved significantly compared with bisphosphonates. Do not count secondary success as passing the primary.
COSMIC showed a numerical reduction in fracture rate versus bisphosphonates without primary-endpoint statistical significance; clinical fracture reduction has not been demonstrated.
DAYBREAK sponsor reported Zenkuda intraocular inflammation 0% and tabirafusp 0.4%, versus aflibercept comparator; these specific observed events do not establish all long-term safety dimensions.
DAYBREAK sponsor reported tabirafusp-ted key anatomical secondary endpoint met at p<0.0001, alongside separate non-inferiority vision primary results; no superiority inference.
DAYBREAK observed Zenkuda vision non-inferiority (p=0.0007) and tabirafusp non-inferiority (p=0.0036) versus aflibercept at year one, not superiority; comparative MCID not independently assessed.

DAYBREAK sponsor reported 54% of Zenkuda-treated participants achieved a 24-week retreatment interval at year one; this is observed treatment-interval durability, not indefinite maintenance of efficacy.
Kodiak described its intention to submit Zenkuda BLA data during fourth quarter 2026; this is a plan, not FDA application acceptance, PDUFA assignment or approval.
